prog-bbm-001.question: In a Boston Scientific dual-chamber pacemaker, what is the principle of the RYTHMIQ algorithm?
options: AAI(R) with slower VVI backup, switching to DDD(R) if AV synchrony is lost
AAI(R) with V backup on the next cycle, DDD(R) if 2 of 4 A-A cycles lack an R
DDD(R) with a periodically extended AV delay to search for intrinsic conduction
ADI(R) while conduction persists, DDD(R) if 3 of 8 cycles lack conduction
commentaires: Correct: RYTHMIQ operates in AAI(R) with a slower VVI backup running in the background and switches to DDD(R) if AV synchrony is lost.
Incorrect: ventricular backup on the next cycle and the 2-of-4 criterion belong to Medtronic MVP.
Incorrect: periodic AV delay extension while remaining in DDD is AV Search+ (or Abbott VIP), not RYTHMIQ itself.
Incorrect: ADI(R) with a return to DDD(R) after 3 of 8 cycles without conduction is Biotronik Vp Suppression.
prog-bbm-001.explication: RYTHMIQ is an algorithm designed to minimise unnecessary ventricular pacing in patients with preserved AV conduction. The device operates in AAI(R) while a VVI backup mode runs in the background at a rate below the lower rate limit: as long as conduction is intact, the ventricle is not paced. If loss of AV synchrony is detected, the device switches to DDD(R), then returns to AAI(R) once conduction resumes. Unlike Medtronic MVP, RYTHMIQ does not need to "drop" QRS complexes to switch to DDD(R). It is only available when the permanent programmed mode is DDD(R). It must not be confused with AV Search+ (AV delay hysteresis, on which it relies to return to AAI(R)) or with Biotronik Vp Suppression (DDD(R) ↔ ADI(R) switching).
prog-bbm-001.aRetenir: RYTHMIQ = AAI(R) with a reduced-rate VVI backup, switching to DDD(R) if AV synchrony is lost.

prog-bbm-002.question: A Boston Scientific pacemaker is programmed DDD with RYTHMIQ on. At what rate does the backup VVI pacing run during the AAI phase if the lower rate limit (LRL) is 60 bpm? And if it is 40 bpm?
prog-bbm-002.reponseAttendue: The VVI backup runs 15 bpm below the LRL, bounded between 30 and 60 bpm: 45 bpm for an LRL of 60; 30 bpm (not 25) for an LRL of 40.
prog-bbm-002.explication: During the AAI(R) phase of RYTHMIQ, the Boston Scientific manual states that backup VVI pacing is delivered 15 bpm below the LRL. This backup rate is bounded: never below 30 bpm and never above 60 bpm. With an LRL of 60, the backup rate is therefore 45 bpm; with an LRL of 40, the raw calculation would give 25, but the lower bound imposes 30 bpm. As long as conduction is present, this VVI mode does not intervene. In practice, this explains why isolated slow ventricular cycles may be seen on a Holter before the switch to DDD(R).
prog-bbm-002.aRetenir: RYTHMIQ VVI backup = LRL − 15 bpm, bounded between 30 and 60 bpm.

prog-bbm-003.question: During the AAI(R) phase of RYTHMIQ, which criterion switches the pacemaker to DDD(R)?
options: Two consecutive blocked P waves with no ventricular event
Six consecutive PR intervals longer than the programmed maximum
3 slow ventricular beats within a window of 11 beats
No ventricular sensed event in 2 of the last 4 A-A cycles
commentaires: Incorrect: 2 consecutive blocked P waves is the complete AV block criterion of MicroPort SafeR.
Incorrect: 6 consecutive excessively long PR intervals is the first-degree AV block criterion of MicroPort SafeR.
Correct: RYTHMIQ switches to DDD(R) when 3 slow beats (at least 150 ms late) occur out of 11.
Incorrect: absence of ventricular sensing in 2 of 4 A-A cycles is the Medtronic MVP criterion.
prog-bbm-003.explication: RYTHMIQ monitors for loss of AV synchrony by counting slow ventricular beats. A slow beat is a ventricular event, sensed or paced, occurring at least 150 ms later than the AAI(R) pacing interval. When 3 slow beats occur within a window of 11 beats, the device switches to DDD(R) and stores a RYTHMIQ episode with 20 s of EGM. The criteria "2 consecutive blocked P waves" and "6 long PR intervals" belong to MicroPort SafeR, and the "2 of 4 A-A cycles without ventricular sensing" criterion to Medtronic MVP. Mixing up manufacturers in this way is a common pitfall in the device clinic.
prog-bbm-003.aRetenir: RYTHMIQ switches to DDD(R) after 3 slow ventricular beats out of 11.

prog-bbm-004.question: In a patient with a Boston Scientific pacemaker and RYTHMIQ on, if AV Search+ is programmed Off, a switch from AAI(R) to DDD(R) occurs only once: the device then remains in DDD(R) until it is reprogrammed.
options: True
False
commentaires: Correct: without AV Search+, nothing tests for recovery of conduction, so after the first switch the device remains in DDD(R).
Incorrect: RYTHMIQ's return to AAI(R) depends on AV Search+; turning it off makes DDD(R) permanent after the first episode.
prog-bbm-004.explication: The return from DDD(R) to AAI(R) with VVI backup relies on AV Search+: if AV Search+ remains in AV hysteresis for at least 25 cycles and fewer than 2 of the last 10 cycles are V-paced, the device returns to AAI(R). Without AV Search+, no mechanism tests for recovery of conduction, so the pacemaker stays in DDD(R). The Boston Scientific manual even presents this as a deliberate option when the switch is intended to occur only once. This is a classic pitfall: turning AV Search+ off "to keep things simple" effectively disables RV pacing reduction after the first episode.
prog-bbm-004.aRetenir: RYTHMIQ's return to AAI(R) depends on AV Search+; without it, DDD(R) becomes permanent.

prog-bbm-005.question: Regarding the AV Search+ algorithm in Boston Scientific pacemakers, which statements are correct?
options: It periodically extends the AV delay (Search AV Delay) for up to 8 cycles to search for intrinsic conduction
It reverts to the programmed AV delay when 2 ventricular paced events occur within a sliding window of 10 cycles
It switches the device to ADI(R) mode as long as intrinsic AV conduction is present
It enforces systematic ventricular pacing during exercise
commentaires: Correct: the Search AV Delay is applied periodically for up to 8 cycles to allow an intrinsic QRS to emerge.
Correct: 2 ventricular paced events within a 10-cycle window trigger a return to the programmed AV delay.
Incorrect: AV Search+ remains in DDD with an extended AV delay; switching to ADI(R) is the principle of Biotronik Vp Suppression.
Incorrect: nothing in AV Search+ enforces ventricular pacing during exercise.
prog-bbm-005.explication: AV Search+ promotes intrinsic AV conduction by allowing an AV delay longer than the programmed one. Periodically (Search Interval), the AV delay is extended for up to 8 cycles; as long as the intrinsic PR intervals remain shorter than the Search AV Delay, hysteresis is maintained. The device reverts to the programmed AV delay if the search finds no intrinsic ventricular activity within 8 cycles, or if 2 ventricular paced events occur within a 10-cycle window. The device stays in DDD: switching to an ADI(R) mode is the principle of Biotronik Vp Suppression. The Search AV Delay must be longer than the maximum paced AV delay, and the programmer does not take it into account when calculating the TARP: if conduction is lost, Wenckebach-type behaviour may appear below the maximum tracking rate.
prog-bbm-005.aRetenir: AV Search+ = AV delay hysteresis that searches for intrinsic conduction and reverts to the programmed delay if the ventricle is paced 2 times in 10 cycles.

prog-bbm-006.question: How does PaceSafe RVAC (Right Ventricular Automatic Capture) work in a Boston Scientific pacemaker?
options: Threshold measured and trended, without ever changing the programmed amplitude
Threshold measured periodically, amplitude at twice threshold, no beat-to-beat check
Threshold measured by the AV conduction or atrial chamber reset method
Daily threshold + 0.5 V, capture confirmed on every beat, backup pulse
commentaires: Incorrect: measuring and trending the threshold without adapting the amplitude is the ATM mode of Biotronik Capture Control.
Incorrect: an amplitude at twice threshold without beat-to-beat verification corresponds to Boston Scientific atrial RAAT, not RVAC.
Incorrect: AV conduction and atrial chamber reset are the two methods of Medtronic Atrial Capture Management.
Correct: RVAC sets the amplitude 0.5 V above the daily threshold, confirms capture on every beat and delivers a backup pulse.
prog-bbm-006.explication: PaceSafe RVAC measures the ventricular threshold every day and sets the amplitude 0.5 V above that threshold (range 0.7 to 3.5 V, pulse width fixed at 0.4 ms). It then confirms capture beat by beat using the evoked response. If loss of capture occurs, a backup pulse of at least 3.5 V is delivered about 70 ms after the primary pulse. If loss of capture is confirmed (2 cycles out of 4), the algorithm is suspended and a new test is performed an hour later. The atrium follows a different logic (RAAT: twice the threshold, without beat-to-beat verification). Threshold monitoring without amplitude adaptation corresponds to Biotronik ATM mode.
prog-bbm-006.aRetenir: RVAC = daily threshold + 0.5 V, capture confirmed on every beat, and a backup pulse if capture is lost.

prog-bbm-007.question: What is the minute ventilation (MV) sensor used for rate response by Boston Scientific based on?
options: Endocardial acceleration measured at the tip of a dedicated lead
Transthoracic impedance, giving respiratory rate and tidal volume
Intracardiac ventricular impedance, reflecting myocardial contractility
An accelerometer measuring vibrations related to physical activity
commentaires: Incorrect: endocardial acceleration measured by a dedicated lead is the MicroPort SonR sensor, used to optimise CRT.
Correct: the MV sensor measures transthoracic impedance; minute ventilation = respiratory rate × tidal volume.
Incorrect: intracardiac impedance, reflecting contractility, is the principle of Biotronik Closed Loop Stimulation.
Incorrect: the accelerometer is a separate, motion-sensitive sensor that can be combined with the MV sensor.
prog-bbm-007.explication: The MV sensor (also called the respiratory sensor) delivers small current pulses and measures transthoracic impedance, which varies with respiration. Minute ventilation, the product of respiratory rate and tidal volume, is used to increase the pacing rate according to physiological demand. The same measurements feed trends such as respiratory rate. The accelerometer is a separate, motion-sensitive sensor that can be combined with MV. Intracardiac ventricular impedance is the signal used by Biotronik Closed Loop Stimulation, and endocardial acceleration that of MicroPort SonR.
prog-bbm-007.aRetenir: MV sensor = transthoracic impedance → respiratory rate × tidal volume.

prog-bbm-008.question: A patient with a Boston Scientific pacemaker with minute ventilation rate response (MV On) is intubated in intensive care. The nurse notes pacing close to the maximum sensor rate with no clinical explanation. What is the appropriate management?
options: Turn off the accelerometer while leaving minute ventilation active
Increase the maximum sensor rate to avoid rate capping
Program the MV sensor Off during mechanical ventilation
Reduce ventricular sensitivity to avoid myopotential oversensing
commentaires: Incorrect: it is the MV sensor, fooled by the ventilator, that is driving the rate; turning off the accelerometer alone changes nothing.
Incorrect: raising the maximum rate would worsen the paced tachycardia without addressing the cause.
Correct: the manual requires the MV sensor to be programmed Off during mechanical ventilation; failing that, a magnet provides asynchronous pacing without rate response.
Incorrect: ventricular sensitivity has nothing to do with the MV sensor; there is no oversensing here.
prog-bbm-008.explication: The Boston Scientific manual states that the MV/respiratory sensor must be programmed Off during mechanical ventilation, otherwise inappropriate sensor-driven rates and misleading respiratory trends may occur. External monitors that inject current (respiratory monitoring, some ECG or haemodynamic monitors) can also distort the impedance measurement and drive the rate up to the maximum sensor rate. If no programmer is available, a magnet provides temporary asynchronous pacing without rate response, provided the magnet response is programmed to asynchronous pacing (Pace Async, the usual setting); the magnet rate then depends on battery status (100 bpm at beginning of life). Turning off only the accelerometer leaves the cause in place, increasing the maximum rate would worsen the problem, and ventricular sensitivity has nothing to do with the sensor.
prog-bbm-008.aRetenir: Mechanical ventilation or impedance-based monitoring: MV sensor Off.

prog-bbm-009.question: What is the purpose of the Rate Smoothing feature in a Boston Scientific pacemaker?
options: Limiting pacing interval changes to a percentage of the last R-R interval
Pacing at a high rate for a programmed period after a sudden drop in rate
Lowering the lower rate during programmed sleep hours
Shortening the escape interval after an ectopic beat to eliminate the pause
commentaires: Correct: Rate Smoothing limits cycle-to-cycle change to 3–25% of the last R-R interval, both upwards and downwards.
Incorrect: this is the principle of Sudden Brady Response (or Medtronic Rate Drop Response), which is incompatible with Rate Smoothing On.
Incorrect: a programmed night-time reduction in rate corresponds to a Sleep-type function, not Rate Smoothing.
Incorrect: eliminating the post-ectopic pause is the principle of Medtronic Rate Stabilization.
prog-bbm-009.explication: Rate Smoothing limits abrupt changes in pacing rate. The allowed change is a percentage of the last R-R interval (3–25% in 3% steps), programmable separately for increases (Rate Smoothing Up) and decreases (Rate Smoothing Down). The feature is useful at the onset and termination of a tracked atrial arrhythmia, in addition to mode switching (ATR): it prevents abrupt rises in the paced rate up to the maximum tracking rate and the associated symptoms. It does not eliminate the post-ectopic pause (the principle of Medtronic Rate Stabilization) and is not a night-time resting rate. Rate Smoothing cannot be programmed On if Sudden Brady Response, which paces at a high rate after a sudden drop in rate, is active.
prog-bbm-009.aRetenir: Rate Smoothing caps the cycle-to-cycle rate change at a percentage of the preceding R-R interval.

prog-bbm-010.question: Regarding Rhythm ID (Boston Scientific ICDs), which statements are correct?
options: It compares the tachycardia EGM with a reference template recorded in sinus rhythm (Vector Timing and Correlation morphology analysis)
In a dual-chamber device, if the ventricular rate exceeds the atrial rate, therapy is delivered without further analysis
It can withhold therapy in the VF zone if the template matches
It relies on beat-by-beat analysis of P-R patterns, without morphology analysis
commentaires: Correct: Rhythm ID compares the tachycardia EGM with an automatically acquired sinus template (Vector Timing and Correlation).
Correct: in a dual-chamber device, V faster than A indicates a ventricular origin and leads directly to therapy.
Incorrect: like all SVT discriminators, Rhythm ID acts only in VT zones, never in the VF zone.
Incorrect: P-R pattern analysis without morphology corresponds to Medtronic PR Logic; Rhythm ID combines morphology and A/V analysis.
prog-bbm-010.explication: Rhythm ID combines morphology analysis (Vector Timing and Correlation, comparing the tachycardia EGM with an automatically acquired sinus rhythm template) with analysis of atrial and ventricular intervals. In a dual-chamber device, a ventricular rate faster than the atrial rate indicates a ventricular origin and leads directly to therapy. Like all SVT discriminators, Rhythm ID acts only in VT zones: it never withholds therapy in the VF zone. P-R pattern analysis without morphology is the logic of Medtronic PR Logic. Boston Scientific's implementation of the 2019 consensus update recommends Rhythm ID in ICDs (Onset/Stability or Rhythm ID in CRT-Ds) and points out that discriminators only apply up to 230 bpm: a VF zone programmed too low therefore deprives fast SVTs of any discrimination. In the RIGHT trial, ICDs using Rhythm ID (VITALITY 2 generation) had more inappropriate therapies than the Medtronic ICDs they were compared with, especially in single-chamber devices and for rhythms < 175 bpm, which argues for high detection rates.
prog-bbm-010.aRetenir: Rhythm ID = morphology correlation with the sinus template + A/V analysis; never inhibits in the VF zone, discrimination limited to 230 bpm.

prog-bbm-011.question: In the Onset/Stability discrimination suite of a Boston Scientific ICD, which criterion mainly targets sinus tachycardia and which targets atrial fibrillation?
prog-bbm-011.reponseAttendue: Onset (suddenness of onset) is used to identify sinus tachycardia, which starts gradually; Stability (regularity of R-R intervals) is used to identify AF, which has an irregular ventricular response.
prog-bbm-011.explication: Sinus tachycardia starts gradually, whereas VT starts abruptly: the Onset criterion exploits this difference. Conducted AF produces irregular R-R intervals, whereas monomorphic VT is usually regular: this is the role of the Stability criterion, which can be combined with the atrial rate threshold (AFib Rate Threshold) in dual-chamber devices. Boston Scientific's implementation of the 2019 consensus update suggests, for CRT-Ds, Onset/Stability or Rhythm ID, with Sustained Rate Duration (SRD) programmed Off. Classic pitfall: a VT starting during exercise-induced sinus tachycardia may fail the Onset criterion and have its therapy withheld; conversely, an active SRD timer would eventually treat a prolonged SVT, hence the recommendation to leave it Off.
prog-bbm-011.aRetenir: Onset discriminates sinus tachycardia; Stability discriminates AF.

prog-bbm-012.question: According to the manufacturer-specific implementation of the 2019 HRS/EHRA/APHRS/LAHRS consensus update on ICD programming, which "prolonged delay" programming (option 1) is suggested for a Boston Scientific ICD in primary prevention, with no history of VT?
options: VF ≥ 231 bpm (30/40 intervals) and VT2 ≥ 188 bpm (30 intervals), VT1 monitor only
VF ≥ 250 bpm (5 s) and VT ≥ 185 bpm (12 s), optional VT-1 monitor zone
VF ≥ 200 bpm (1 s) and VT ≥ 170 bpm (2.5 s), with ATP in the VT zone
A single therapy zone at 200 bpm, with a duration of 2.5 s
commentaires: Incorrect: 231 bpm with 30/40 and 188 bpm with 30 intervals are the settings of the Biotronik implementation.
Correct: option 1: VF 250 bpm (8/10 + 5 s), VT 185 bpm (8/10 + 12 s), VT-1 as a monitor zone at the operator's discretion.
Incorrect: short detection (1 s) at a low rate is the conventional programming that the consensus aims to avoid.
Incorrect: high-rate therapy (200 bpm, 2.5 s) corresponds to option 2 in the appendix, not to the "prolonged delay" option.
prog-bbm-012.explication: The manufacturer appendix (Appendix B) of the 2019 update translates the principles of the 2015 consensus into Boston Scientific settings. Option 1 (prolonged delay): VF at 250 bpm with 8/10 intervals plus a 5 s duration, VT at 185 bpm with 8/10 plus a 12 s duration, VT-1 as a monitor zone at the operator's discretion. Option 2 (high-rate therapy): VF at 200 bpm with a 2.5 s duration. These options are based on MADIT-RIT, conducted with Boston Scientific ICDs: compared with conventional programming, both high-rate therapy (≥ 200 bpm) and delayed therapy reduced inappropriate therapies by about 75%, with a significant mortality reduction for high-rate therapy (HR 0.45) and a borderline significant one for prolonged delay (HR 0.56; p = 0.06). SVT discriminators only apply up to 230 bpm. Settings expressed as numbers of intervals (231 bpm with 30/40) belong to the Biotronik implementation, and rapid detection with a 1 s duration corresponds to the conventional programming that should be avoided.
prog-bbm-012.aRetenir: Boston Scientific, primary prevention: VT 185 bpm/12 s and VF 250 bpm/5 s, or high-rate therapy with VF 200 bpm/2.5 s.

prog-bbm-013.question: Which of the following parameters are combined in the HeartLogic index (Boston Scientific CRT-D/ICD) to predict heart failure decompensation?
options: Heart sounds (S1, S3)
AF burden and ventricular rate during AF
Thoracic impedance and night-time resting heart rate
Pulmonary artery pressure measured by an implanted sensor
commentaires: Correct: heart sounds S1 and S3, recorded by the accelerometer, are a cornerstone of the index.
Incorrect: AF burden and ventricular rate during AF are parameters of the Medtronic TriageHF score, not HeartLogic.
Correct: thoracic impedance and night-time heart rate are part of the index, together with respiration and activity.
Incorrect: pulmonary artery pressure requires a sensor implanted in the pulmonary artery, separate from HeartLogic.
prog-bbm-013.explication: HeartLogic calculates a daily composite index from sensors in the device: heart sounds recorded by the accelerometer (S1, S3), respiration (rate and the ratio of respiratory rate to tidal volume), thoracic impedance, night-time heart rate and activity. The alert is triggered when the index exceeds a configurable threshold. AF burden is part of the Medtronic TriageHF score, not HeartLogic. Pulmonary artery pressure is measured by a different device (a sensor implanted in the pulmonary artery). In practice, a HeartLogic alert should prompt a clinical assessment for congestion (weight, breathlessness, adherence, renal function) rather than a change in treatment based on the index alone.
prog-bbm-013.aRetenir: HeartLogic = heart sounds + respiration + thoracic impedance + night-time heart rate + activity.

prog-bbm-014.question: What were the main validation results of the HeartLogic algorithm in the MultiSENSE study (sensitivity, unexplained alert rate, lead time)?
prog-bbm-014.reponseAttendue: In the validation cohort: 70% sensitivity for detecting a heart failure event, 1.47 unexplained alerts per patient-year, and a median lead time of about 34 days between alert and event.
prog-bbm-014.explication: MultiSENSE enrolled 900 patients with CRT-Ds, with a development cohort and an independent validation cohort. The two primary endpoints were a sensitivity above 40% and fewer than 2 unexplained alerts per patient-year; both were comfortably met (70% and 1.47/patient-year). The alert preceded the heart failure event by a median of 34 days, leaving time to intervene. A subsequent analysis showed that the event rate is about 10 times higher during an alert period than outside it. This was a diagnostic validation study, not a trial demonstrating clinical benefit.
prog-bbm-014.aRetenir: HeartLogic (MultiSENSE): 70% sensitivity, 1.47 unexplained alerts/patient-year, median lead time of 34 days.

prog-bbm-015.question: What was the main result of the SMART-AV trial, which evaluated Boston Scientific's SmartDelay algorithm for AV delay optimisation in CRT?
options: SmartDelay outperformed echo and a fixed delay on LV end-systolic volume
Echo-guided optimisation outperformed both SmartDelay and a fixed delay
SmartDelay was non-inferior to echo, with fewer HF hospitalisations
Neither SmartDelay nor echo outperformed a fixed 120 ms AV delay
commentaires: Incorrect: no difference was observed in LV end-systolic volume at 6 months.
Incorrect: echocardiography did not outperform SmartDelay or the fixed delay.
Incorrect: non-inferiority with fewer HF hospitalisations is the result of RESPOND-CRT (MicroPort SonR).
Correct: SmartDelay, echocardiography and a fixed 120 ms AV delay gave identical results.
prog-bbm-015.explication: SmartDelay calculates an AV delay from intervals measured on the intracardiac electrograms, without echocardiography. In SMART-AV (980 randomised patients), the primary endpoint was the change in LV end-systolic volume at 6 months. There was no difference between SmartDelay, echocardiography and a fixed 120 ms AV delay, nor in the secondary endpoints. The conclusion is that routine AV delay optimisation is not justified in all patients, although it may still have a role in non-responders. Not to be confused with RESPOND-CRT, in which MicroPort SonR optimisation was non-inferior to echocardiography. SmartDelay remains a quick and reproducible tool, suggested in the manufacturer-specific implementation of the ICD consensus.
prog-bbm-015.aRetenir: SMART-AV: for routine optimisation, neither SmartDelay nor echocardiography does better than a fixed 120 ms AV delay.

prog-bbm-016.question: In the ALTITUDE study, patients with Boston Scientific ICDs/CRT-Ds followed on the LATITUDE remote monitoring network had better survival than those followed in clinic only, which formally proves that remote monitoring reduces mortality.
options: True
False
commentaires: Incorrect: ALTITUDE is an observational registry; the association with better survival does not prove causality.
Correct: remotely monitored patients may differ in unmeasured factors; only randomised trials establish causality.
prog-bbm-016.explication: ALTITUDE is a very large observational analysis (more than 185,000 patients): survival at 1 and 5 years was better in patients remotely monitored on LATITUDE than in those followed in clinic only. As a non-randomised registry, this association does not prove causality: remotely monitored patients may differ in unmeasured factors (adherence, social support, medical follow-up). The study also showed that receiving a shock was associated with increased mortality. Remote monitoring is now recommended for all ICD/CRT recipients, based on the totality of the evidence, including randomised data.
prog-bbm-016.aRetenir: ALTITUDE shows an association between LATITUDE and better survival, not causal proof (observational registry).

prog-bbm-017.question: Regarding the EMBLEM S-ICD subcutaneous ICD (Boston Scientific), which statements are correct?
options: It delivers a non-programmable 80 J biphasic shock
It does not deliver antitachycardia pacing (ATP)
It provides no permanent bradycardia pacing; only optional post-shock pacing at 50 bpm for up to 30 s is available
It requires a transvenous right ventricular lead for sensing
commentaires: Correct: the S-ICD delivers a non-programmable 80 J biphasic shock.
Correct: the S-ICD does not deliver ATP; recurrent monomorphic VT amenable to ATP is a practical contraindication.
Correct: only optional post-shock pacing (50 bpm, up to 30 s) exists; there is no permanent bradycardia pacing.
Incorrect: the S-ICD is entirely extrathoracic, with no transvenous lead at all.
prog-bbm-017.explication: The S-ICD is entirely extrathoracic: a parasternal subcutaneous electrode connected to a generator in a lateral thoracic position, with no transvenous lead at all. Its only response to a detected ventricular tachyarrhythmia is a non-programmable 80 J biphasic shock. There is neither ATP nor permanent bradycardia pacing; optional post-shock pacing is delivered at 50 bpm for up to 30 s. Hence the practical contraindications: a need for bradycardia pacing, CRT, or recurrent monomorphic VT amenable to ATP.
prog-bbm-017.aRetenir: S-ICD: non-programmable 80 J shock, no ATP or permanent pacing, only 30 s of post-shock pacing.

prog-bbm-018.question: In a Boston Scientific S-ICD, what is the difference between the Shock Zone and the Conditional Shock Zone?
options: Shock Zone: 80 J shock; Conditional Zone: lower-energy shock
Conditional Zone: monitoring only, no shock; Shock Zone: therapy
Conditional Zone: ATP then shock; Shock Zone: immediate shock
Shock Zone: rate only; Conditional Zone: rate + morphology
commentaires: Incorrect: the S-ICD shock is always 80 J and non-programmable.
Incorrect: the Conditional Zone does deliver therapy, but only after discrimination; a monitor-only zone is an option of transvenous ICDs.
Incorrect: the S-ICD never delivers ATP, whatever the zone.
Correct: in the Shock Zone, rate alone decides; in the Conditional Zone, morphology and QRS width are added.
prog-bbm-018.explication: The S-ICD allows two rate zones. In the Shock Zone (170 to 250 bpm), rate is the only criterion. In the Conditional Shock Zone, which must be lower (170 to 240 bpm), the device compares complexes with the sinus rhythm template acquired at set-up and analyses QRS width and whether the rhythm is polymorphic, so as not to treat AF, sinus tachycardia or other SVTs. Rate is estimated from the running average of the last 4 R-R intervals, and charging only starts if 18 of the last 24 intervals are classified as "treatable", then confirmed by the persistence analysis. The manual advises programming one of the zones at 200 bpm or below to ensure VF detection. The S-ICD does not deliver ATP.
prog-bbm-018.aRetenir: S-ICD: Shock Zone = rate only; Conditional Zone = rate + morphology.

prog-bbm-019.question: What is the role of the SMART Pass filter in the Boston Scientific S-ICD?
options: Automatic selection of the best of the three available sensing vectors
An extra high-pass filter against oversensing, mainly of T waves
A discrimination zone based on comparison with the sinus rhythm template
Post-shock pacing at 50 bpm for up to 30 seconds
commentaires: Incorrect: the sensing vector is selected during automatic set-up; SMART Pass is a filter applied to the signal.
Correct: SMART Pass attenuates low-frequency signals (T wave); it is enabled if the signal is at least 0.5 mV and disabled if undersensing is suspected.
Incorrect: comparison with the sinus template is the Conditional Shock Zone analysis, not SMART Pass.
Incorrect: post-shock pacing (50 bpm, up to 30 s) is a separate S-ICD option.
prog-bbm-019.explication: Most inappropriate S-ICD shocks result from cardiac oversensing, particularly QRS-T wave double counting. SMART Pass adds a high-pass filter that attenuates low-frequency signals while preserving an adequate sensing margin. It is enabled automatically during set-up if the subcutaneous ECG signal amplitude is at least 0.5 mV, and then disabled by the device if undersensing is suspected: set-up must then be repeated to re-enable it. In the prospective evaluation by Theuns et al., SMART Pass reduced the risk of a first inappropriate shock by 50% and the risk of all inappropriate shocks by 68%, without delaying appropriate shocks.
prog-bbm-019.aRetenir: SMART Pass = the S-ICD's high-pass anti-oversensing filter, which roughly halves inappropriate shocks.

prog-bbm-020.question: During pre-implant ECG screening for an S-ICD (manual or automated screening tool), under what condition is the patient considered eligible?
prog-bbm-020.reponseAttendue: At least one surface lead (corresponding to an S-ICD sensing vector) must be acceptable in all tested postures: every QRS complex and T wave assessed must fit within the coloured template, with a stable morphology from one posture to another.
prog-bbm-020.explication: Screening reproduces the subcutaneous sensing vectors using surface electrodes placed according to the manufacturer's diagram. Each lead is assessed with the coloured template (manual tool 4744) or by the automated screening tool (AST): the QRS and T wave must stay within the profile chosen according to QRS amplitude. A lead is acceptable only if it passes in all tested postures (e.g. supine and standing), with a stable morphology. The patient is eligible if at least one lead is acceptable in all postures. Failure carries a risk of inaccurate sensing and inappropriate shocks due to T-wave oversensing.
prog-bbm-020.aRetenir: S-ICD: eligible if at least one vector is acceptable in all tested postures.

prog-bbm-021.question: According to the manufacturer-specific implementation of the 2019 ICD programming consensus update, which zone settings are suggested for the S-ICD?
options: Shock ≥ 230 bpm, conditional ≥ 200 bpm (or 10–20 bpm below the known VT)
Conditional ≥ 150 bpm to treat slow VTs as well, shock ≥ 200 bpm
Shock ≥ 200 bpm and conditional ≥ 180 bpm, without post-shock pacing
A single shock zone ≥ 170 bpm, conditional zone disabled so nothing is missed
commentaires: Correct: Shock Zone ≥ 230 bpm, Conditional Zone ≥ 200 bpm or 10 to 20 bpm below the known VT, and post-shock pacing to be considered.
Incorrect: S-ICD zones start at 170 bpm, and a 150 bpm zone would multiply inappropriate shocks.
Incorrect: these cut-offs are too low; the appendix in fact suggests considering post-shock pacing.
Incorrect: a single 170 bpm zone without discrimination would expose the patient to inappropriate shocks for sinus tachycardia or AF.
prog-bbm-021.explication: The Boston Scientific appendix of the 2019 update suggests, for the S-ICD, a Shock Zone of at least 230 bpm and a Conditional Zone of at least 200 bpm, or 10 to 20 bpm below the VT if its rate is known. It also advises considering post-shock pacing. Enabling the Conditional Zone with morphology discrimination reduces inappropriate shocks: in UNTOUCHED, with rate-only therapy above 250 bpm and discrimination between 200 and 250 bpm, 95.9% of patients had received no inappropriate shock at 18 months. A single 170 bpm zone without discrimination would expose the patient to numerous inappropriate shocks for sinus tachycardia or AF.
prog-bbm-021.aRetenir: S-ICD: Conditional Zone around 200 bpm with discrimination, high Shock Zone (≥ 230–250 bpm).

prog-bbm-022.question: What was the main result of the PRAETORIAN trial, which compared the S-ICD with the transvenous ICD in patients without a pacing indication?
options: Twice as many device-related complications with the S-ICD
Fewer inappropriate shocks with the S-ICD thanks to the SMART Pass filter
Non-inferiority of the S-ICD for complications + inappropriate shocks
Superiority of the S-ICD for all-cause mortality, with 40% fewer deaths
commentaires: Incorrect: on the contrary, complications tended to be less frequent with the S-ICD.
Incorrect: inappropriate shocks were slightly more frequent with the S-ICD, with no significant difference.
Correct: 15.1% vs 15.7% at 48 months for the composite of complications + inappropriate shocks: non-inferiority established.
Incorrect: no difference in mortality was demonstrated.
prog-bbm-022.explication: PRAETORIAN randomised 849 patients with an ICD indication but no pacing indication. With a median follow-up of about 49 months, the composite endpoint (device-related complications and inappropriate shocks) occurred at a similar rate in both arms (15.1% vs 15.7% at 48 months), establishing non-inferiority of the S-ICD. Complications tended to be less frequent with the S-ICD and inappropriate shocks slightly more frequent, with no significant difference. No difference in mortality was demonstrated. These data support the S-ICD as an alternative to the transvenous ICD when there is no need for bradycardia pacing, ATP or CRT (ESC 2022).
prog-bbm-022.aRetenir: PRAETORIAN: S-ICD non-inferior to the transvenous ICD for complications + inappropriate shocks.

prog-bbm-023.question: What is the principle underlying Closed Loop Stimulation (CLS) rate response in Biotronik pacemakers?
options: Intracardiac ventricular impedance during each contraction
Minute ventilation, derived from respiratory transthoracic impedance
Endocardial acceleration measured at the tip of a dedicated lead
An accelerometer in the can, sensitive to chest wall movement
commentaires: Correct: CLS measures unipolar RV tip-to-can impedance during each contraction, reflecting contractility.
Incorrect: minute ventilation is the Boston Scientific rate response sensor.
Incorrect: endocardial acceleration is the MicroPort SonR signal, used to optimise CRT.
Incorrect: Biotronik devices also have an accelerometer, but as a separate sensor; CLS uses it only to identify rest.
prog-bbm-023.explication: CLS measures unipolar intracardiac impedance between the tip of the ventricular lead and the can during each contraction. Changes in this impedance curve reflect myocardial contractility (inotropy), which is controlled by the same autonomic nervous system as the sinus node. Rate response therefore reacts not only to physical activity but also to mental stress, which sets it apart from motion sensors. It works with standard leads and initialises automatically. Biotronik devices also have an accelerometer (R modes), but as a separate sensor; CLS uses it only to identify periods of rest. Minute ventilation (Boston Scientific) and endocardial acceleration (MicroPort SonR) are different signals.
prog-bbm-023.aRetenir: CLS = intracardiac ventricular impedance, reflecting contractility, responding to both physical and mental stress.

prog-bbm-024.question: A 52-year-old woman has recurrent, frequent reflex syncope causing injury, with a cardioinhibitory response on tilt testing (asystole > 3 s). A decision is made to implant a pacemaker. Which programming is supported by the randomised SPAIN trial?
options: VVI at 40 bpm with rate hysteresis
DDD with Rate Drop Response
DDD with Closed Loop Stimulation (DDD-CLS)
AAI(R) with accelerometer-based rate response
commentaires: Incorrect: VVI loses AV synchrony and does not respond early to the phase preceding syncope.
Incorrect: Medtronic Rate Drop Response was evaluated in the double-blind VPS II trial, with no significant reduction in syncope.
Correct: in SPAIN, 72% of patients in DDD-CLS had at least a 50% reduction in syncope, versus 28% in placebo mode.
Incorrect: AAI is ineffective against the cardioinhibitory component, which often involves paroxysmal AV block.
prog-bbm-024.explication: SPAIN was a double-blind crossover trial in patients aged 40 years or older with highly recurrent vasovagal syncope and a cardioinhibitory response on tilt testing. It compared DDD-CLS pacing with a placebo DDI mode at 30 bpm. The proportion of patients with at least a 50% reduction in syncope was 72% with DDD-CLS versus 28% in placebo mode. The presumed advantage of CLS is that it detects the increase in contractility preceding the vasodepressor phase and raises the pacing rate before the heart rate falls. Medtronic Rate Drop Response showed no significant benefit under double-blind conditions (VPS II). VVI is unsuitable (loss of AV synchrony, no early response), and AAI is ineffective against the cardioinhibitory component.
prog-bbm-024.aRetenir: Selected cardioinhibitory reflex syncope: DDD-CLS (SPAIN trial).

prog-bbm-025.question: How does the CLS algorithm build its resting reference to detect an increase in demand?
options: A single curve recorded during initialisation at implant
Monthly manual calibration with an exercise test in clinic
The mean sinus rate over the last 24 hours, taken as rest
The mean of the last 256 rest curves, Vp and Vs separately
commentaires: Incorrect: a curve frozen since implant would not track changes in the patient; the reference is updated continuously.
Incorrect: CLS initialises and adapts automatically, without exercise-test calibration.
Incorrect: CLS is not anchored to the sinus rate but to resting impedance curves.
Correct: the resting reference averages the last 256 curves recorded at rest (identified by the accelerometer), separately for Vp and Vs.
prog-bbm-025.explication: Biotronik's CLS practical guide describes three steps: building the resting curves, comparing them with the curve of the current cycle (load curve), then automatic adaptations. The resting reference curves are continuously updated from the last 256 curves recorded at rest, rest being identified by the accelerometer. They are kept separate for paced and sensed ventricular events. The difference between the current-cycle curve and the reference is converted into a pacing rate. No manual exercise-test calibration is needed, and a curve frozen since implant would not track changes in the patient.
prog-bbm-025.aRetenir: CLS compares each impedance curve with a continuously updated resting reference (256 curves, paced and sensed kept separate).

prog-bbm-026.question: What does the Vp Suppression feature of a Biotronik dual-chamber pacemaker do when intrinsic AV conduction is present?
options: Switches to AAI(R) with a VVI backup running at a reduced rate
Switches from DDD(R) to ADI(R) to avoid unnecessary ventricular pacing
Shortens the AV delay as soon as an intrinsic QRS occurs, to maintain V pacing
Extends the AV delay (positive AV hysteresis) to allow conduction through
commentaires: Incorrect: AAI(R) with a reduced-rate VVI backup is Boston Scientific RYTHMIQ.
Correct: when conduction is present, Vp Suppression switches from DDD(R) to ADI(R); the ventricle is only monitored.
Incorrect: shortening the AV delay to maintain V pacing is negative AV hysteresis, useful in CRT; the effect is the opposite.
Incorrect: positive AV hysteresis is IRSplus, the other Biotronik option; Vp Suppression changes mode.
prog-bbm-026.explication: Vp Suppression is Biotronik's algorithm for minimising ventricular pacing. When intrinsic conduction is present, the device switches from DDD(R) to ADI(R): the atrium is paced or sensed and the ventricle is only monitored. If conduction deteriorates, it returns to DDD(R) to provide ventricular pacing. The principle is similar to Boston Scientific RYTHMIQ or MicroPort SafeR, but the switching criteria are specific to each manufacturer. IRSplus, the other Biotronik option, remains in DDD and extends the AV delay (positive hysteresis). Shortening the AV delay would have the opposite effect, increasing RV pacing.
prog-bbm-026.aRetenir: Vp Suppression = DDD(R) → ADI(R) switch as long as intrinsic AV conduction is present.

prog-bbm-027.question: In a Biotronik pacemaker from the Edora family, what are the standard settings of the Vp Suppression parameters?
options: Return to DDD if 2 of the last 4 A-A cycles have no Vs, no other setting
On by default at implant, with no programmable parameters
ADI after 6 consecutive Vs; return to DDD if 3 of 8 cycles lack conduction
ADI after 12 consecutive Vs; return to DDD after 2 consecutive blocked P waves
commentaires: Incorrect: 2 of 4 A-A cycles without ventricular sensing is the Medtronic MVP switching criterion.
Incorrect: Vp Suppression is Off as standard, and two parameters are programmable once it is enabled.
Correct: pacing suppression after 6 consecutive Vs (1 to 8), pacing resumed if 3 of 8 cycles lack conduction (1 to 4).
Incorrect: 12 intrinsic R waves and 2 consecutive blocked P waves are MicroPort SafeR criteria.
prog-bbm-027.explication: In the Edora 8 technical manual, Vp Suppression is Off as standard. Once enabled, two parameters govern it: pacing suppression after x consecutive Vs (1 to 8, standard 6) and pacing resumption after x of 8 cycles (1 to 4, standard 3). In other words, ventricular pacing is abandoned once conduction has been confirmed over 6 cycles, then resumed if 3 of 8 cycles show loss of conduction. The criteria "2 consecutive blocked P waves" and "12 intrinsic R waves" belong to MicroPort SafeR, and "2 of 4 cycles" to Medtronic MVP. Keeping these algorithms apart is essential to interpret a Holter or a stored EGM correctly.
prog-bbm-027.aRetenir: Vp Suppression (Edora standard): ADI after 6 consecutive Vs, return to DDD if 3 of 8 cycles lack conduction.

prog-bbm-028.question: What is the purpose of the IRSplus (Intrinsic Rhythm Support) feature in Biotronik devices?
options: Promoting intrinsic AV conduction through positive AV hysteresis
Shortening the AV delay to maintain biventricular pacing
Supporting the intrinsic rhythm by lowering the basic rate at night
Switching to ADI(R) as soon as intrinsic AV conduction is confirmed
commentaires: Correct: IRSplus extends the AV delay (positive hysteresis) to allow intrinsic conduction to emerge.
Incorrect: shortening the AV delay for CRT is negative AV hysteresis, the opposite of IRSplus.
Incorrect: despite its name, IRSplus does not act on the basic rate; a night-time reduction is the job of a night rate function.
Incorrect: switching to ADI(R) is Vp Suppression, the other Biotronik algorithm for minimising RV pacing.
prog-bbm-028.explication: IRSplus is a positive AV hysteresis option designed to allow intrinsic conduction to emerge by extending the AV delay. It is an alternative to Vp Suppression (which switches to ADI(R)) for minimising RV pacing in patients with preserved or intermittent conduction. The 2019 ICD consensus update in fact mentions it in its Biotronik implementation ("DDD, consider IRS Plus"). Conversely, negative AV hysteresis is used in CRT to maintain ventricular pacing. Despite its name (Intrinsic Rhythm Support), it does not act on the basic rate. A very long AV delay may, however, promote poorly tolerated AV dyssynchrony, which should be watched for in patients with a very long PR interval.
prog-bbm-028.aRetenir: IRSplus = positive AV hysteresis to promote intrinsic conduction.

prog-bbm-029.question: In a Biotronik device, the Capture Control (Active Capture Control) parameter offers the settings ON, OFF and ATM. What does ATM stand for?
options: Atrial Tachycardia Management: ATP delivered for atrial tachycardias
Automatic Threshold Monitoring: threshold trended, amplitude unchanged
Auto Threshold Margin: amplitude = measured threshold plus a safety margin
Auto-Test Magnet: threshold test triggered by applying a magnet
commentaires: Incorrect: Capture Control is a threshold function, unrelated to the treatment of atrial tachycardias.
Correct: in ATM mode, the threshold is measured and trended without changing the programmed amplitude.
Incorrect: adapting the amplitude to the threshold plus a margin is ON mode, not ATM.
Incorrect: a magnet triggers a threshold test in some devices, but that is not what ATM means.
prog-bbm-029.explication: Capture Control automatically measures the pacing threshold in each chamber with a lead. In ON mode, it adapts the amplitude to the measured threshold plus a programmable safety margin; in ATM mode (monitoring only), it simply measures and trends the threshold, without changing the programmed amplitude. This mode is useful when a fixed amplitude is preferred (recently implanted lead, doubts about measurement reliability) while still tracking threshold changes, particularly on remote monitoring. For the LV in CRT, Capture Control is also available with threshold tracking or ATM.
prog-bbm-029.aRetenir: Capture Control: ON = measurement + amplitude adaptation; ATM = measurement and trending only.

prog-bbm-030.question: In the SMART Detection algorithm of Biotronik dual-chamber ICDs, what is the decision when the averaged ventricular rate is faster than the atrial rate?
options: R-R stability and A/V ratio analysed before any decision
Onset criterion and PR stability analysed before any decision
QRS morphology compared with the reference before any decision
VT counter incremented, no other test; VT therapy given
commentaires: Incorrect: R-R stability and the A/V ratio are tested when the atrium is faster than the ventricle.
Incorrect: onset and PP and PR stability are used in the decision trees for a 1:1 ratio.
Incorrect: morphology comparison is MorphMatch, which cannot be enabled together with SMART.
Correct: V faster than A indicates a ventricular origin; the VT counter is incremented without further testing.
prog-bbm-030.explication: SMART Detection continuously compares atrial and ventricular intervals, each averaged over 4 intervals. If the ventricular rate exceeds the atrial rate, the ICD increments the VT counter without further testing: dissociation with V faster than A indicates a ventricular origin. If A is faster than V, a supraventricular origin is presumed, with exceptions tested by R-R stability and the A/V ratio. With a 1:1 ratio, specific decision trees use the onset criterion and PP and PR stability. SMART applies only to the VT1 and VT2 zones, never to the VF zone.
prog-bbm-030.aRetenir: SMART: V > A = VT with no further test; discrimination applies only in VT zones.

prog-bbm-031.question: Regarding the SMART Detection and MorphMatch discriminators of Biotronik ICDs, which statements are correct?
options: SMART Detection and MorphMatch cannot be enabled at the same time
SMART Detection is mainly intended for single-chamber detection, MorphMatch being the method of choice in multi-chamber devices
MorphMatch can withhold therapy in the VF zone if the morphology matches
MorphMatch requires a functioning atrial lead
commentaires: Correct: the Rivacor manual states that either MorphMatch or SMART Detection is programmed, never both.
Incorrect: it is the other way round: SMART relies on the A/V relationship and suits multi-chamber devices; MorphMatch is mainly used in single-chamber devices.
Incorrect: like the other discriminators, MorphMatch acts only in VT zones, never in the VF zone.
Incorrect: MorphMatch analyses the ventricular signal alone and does not require an atrial lead.
prog-bbm-031.explication: The Rivacor manual states that either MorphMatch or SMART Detection is programmed, never both. MorphMatch compares the QRS morphology of the tachycardia with a reference of conducted rhythm; it is mainly used for single-chamber detection (notably VR-T DX) but remains available in multi-chamber devices. SMART, which relies on the relationship between atrium and ventricle, is the method of choice in dual-chamber devices and CRT-Ds. Like the other discriminators, MorphMatch does not act in the VF zone. It does not require an atrial lead, since it analyses the ventricular signal alone. The Biotronik implementation of the 2019 consensus recommends MorphMatch in single-chamber devices and SMART in dual-chamber devices/CRT-Ds.
prog-bbm-031.aRetenir: Biotronik: MorphMatch (morphology, single-chamber) or SMART (A/V relationship, multi-chamber), never both, and never in the VF zone.

prog-bbm-032.question: With SMART Detection (Biotronik), when an R-R interval in the VT zone is classified as supraventricular in origin, the VT counter is not simply frozen: it is decremented (by 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 4 depending on the case).
options: True
False
commentaires: Correct: a ventricular cycle increments the counter by 1, and a supraventricular cycle decrements it by 0.25 to 4 depending on the branch.
Incorrect: the counter is not frozen; this up/down counting gradually moves the ICD away from the threshold during a prolonged SVT.
prog-bbm-032.explication: The SMART algorithm classifies each R-R interval in the VT zone as ventricular or supraventricular. An interval of ventricular origin increments the VT counter by 1; an interval of atrial origin decrements it by 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 4 depending on the branch of the decision tree. This "up/down" counting explains why a prolonged SVT gradually moves the ICD away from the detection threshold, whereas a clear-cut VT reaches it quickly. The preset SMART values are 20% for onset and 12% for stability. Understanding this counter helps when analysing an episode in which therapy was delayed or withheld.
prog-bbm-032.aRetenir: SMART: +1 for a ventricular cycle, decrement (0.25 to 4) for a supraventricular cycle.

prog-bbm-033.question: According to the Biotronik implementation of the 2019 ICD programming consensus update, which detection programming is suggested in a patient with no history of VT?
options: VF: 8/12 intervals at 200 bpm; VT: 16 intervals at 150 bpm with ATP
VF ≥ 250 bpm (5 s), VT ≥ 185 bpm (12 s), optional VT-1 monitor zone
VF > 255 bpm, fast VT 230 bpm, VT 185 bpm (20 or 30 cycles + 6/8 majority)
VF 231 bpm (30/40 or 24/30), VT2 188 bpm (30 intervals), VT1 monitor
commentaires: Incorrect: short detection at a low rate is the conventional programming that the consensus aims to avoid.
Incorrect: 250 bpm (5 s) and 185 bpm (12 s) are the settings of the Boston Scientific implementation.
Incorrect: 255 bpm, 230 bpm and the 6/8 majority are the settings of the MicroPort implementation.
Correct: VF 231 bpm with 30/40 (otherwise 24/30), VT2 188 bpm with 30 intervals, VT1 as an optional monitor zone.
prog-bbm-033.explication: The Biotronik appendix of the 2019 update suggests, with no history of VT: VF at 231 bpm with 30/40 intervals if programmable (otherwise 24/30), VT2 at 188 bpm with 30 intervals, and VT1 as an optional monitor zone. VF therapy comprises ATP One Shot (1 burst of 8 pulses at 88% of the cycle length) followed by full-energy shocks. For discriminators: MorphMatch in single-chamber devices, SMART in dual-chamber devices/CRT-Ds, Home Monitoring enabled. For dual-chamber pacing, the appendix suggests DDD with IRS Plus (± CLS) or DDD with Vp Suppression. Each manufacturer has its own implementation (in seconds for Boston Scientific, in cycles with a 6/8 majority for MicroPort). Prolonging detection and raising rate cut-offs reduces inappropriate therapies without increasing mortality, as shown by MADIT-RIT and subsequent studies.
prog-bbm-033.aRetenir: Biotronik 2019: VF 231 bpm (30/40), VT2 188 bpm (30 intervals), VT1 monitor zone.

prog-bbm-034.question: With Biotronik Home Monitoring, the daily data transmission only takes place if the patient manually triggers it from the transmitter.
options: True
False
commentaires: Incorrect: the daily transmission is automatic; the patient does not need to trigger anything.
Correct: the device sends its data automatically every day to the CardioMessenger transmitter, with no action required from the patient.
prog-bbm-034.explication: This is false. Home Monitoring relies on an automatic daily transmission from the device to the transmitter (CardioMessenger), which relays the data to the secure platform reviewed by the team. It transmits, among other things, ongoing arrhythmias, thresholds, sensing amplitudes and impedances, pacing statistics and EGMs. Event-triggered messages complement the daily transmission. The patient has nothing to do, provided the transmitter is plugged in and placed close enough. Remote monitoring does not replace a clinic visit in the event of new symptoms.
prog-bbm-034.aRetenir: Home Monitoring = automatic daily transmission, with no patient involvement.

prog-bbm-035.question: What were the two main results of the TRUST trial (Biotronik ICDs with daily Home Monitoring)?
prog-bbm-035.reponseAttendue: An approximately 45% reduction in in-hospital ICD evaluations without any increase in morbidity, and much faster detection of arrhythmic events (median delay < 2 days versus 36 days with conventional follow-up).
prog-bbm-035.explication: TRUST randomised 1,339 ICD patients (2:1) to automatic daily Home Monitoring or conventional in-clinic follow-up. Home Monitoring reduced in-hospital evaluations by 45%, with no excess morbidity: 85.8% of the 6-, 9- and 12-month checks could be carried out remotely only. The median delay between the occurrence of an arrhythmic event and its evaluation by the physician fell from 36 days to less than 2 days. This trial provided strong support for the idea that remote monitoring can replace some routine clinic visits, an idea taken up in the 2023 consensus statement on remote monitoring.
prog-bbm-035.aRetenir: TRUST: −45% hospital visits, and events reviewed in < 2 days instead of 36.

prog-bbm-036.question: In heart failure patients with Biotronik dual-chamber ICDs or CRT-Ds, what did the IN-TIME trial of daily multiparameter remote monitoring show?
options: More HF hospitalisations, related to the excess of transmitted alerts
Fewer patients worsened on the composite score (18.9% vs 27.2%)
Fewer inappropriate shocks, with no effect on heart failure
No significant difference in the composite score or in mortality
commentaires: Incorrect: remote monitoring did not increase hospitalisations; the clinical score improved.
Correct: at 1 year, 18.9% of remotely monitored patients had worsened versus 27.2% of controls, with fewer deaths.
Incorrect: the reduction in inappropriate shocks was studied in other trials (ECOST); IN-TIME focused on heart failure.
Incorrect: the composite score was improved (p = 0.013), with 10 deaths versus 27.
prog-bbm-036.explication: IN-TIME randomised 664 patients (NYHA II–III, LVEF ≤ 35%) to automatic daily multiparameter remote monitoring or standard care. The primary endpoint was a composite score combining death, heart failure hospitalisation, change in NYHA class and patient global self-assessment. At 1 year, 18.9% of remotely monitored patients had a worsened score versus 27.2% of controls (p = 0.013), with 10 deaths versus 27. Daily transmission and a structured response to alerts are probably the key ingredients, whereas other, less responsive remote monitoring trials were negative.
prog-bbm-036.aRetenir: IN-TIME: daily Biotronik remote monitoring improves the composite clinical score in heart failure patients.

prog-bbm-037.question: What is a Biotronik "DX" ICD system?
options: A single-chamber ICD whose lead carries a floating atrial dipole
A dual-chamber ICD with an atrial lead and a defibrillation lead
A fully subcutaneous ICD, with no transvenous lead at all
A dual-chamber leadless pacemaker made up of two capsules
commentaires: Correct: a single defibrillation lead carries, at atrial level, a floating dipole that senses atrial activity.
Incorrect: the whole point of DX is to avoid an atrial lead while still recording atrial activity.
Incorrect: the fully subcutaneous ICD is the S-ICD (Boston Scientific).
Incorrect: the two-capsule leadless pacemaker is the Aveir DR (Abbott).
prog-bbm-037.explication: The DX system combines a dedicated ICD with a ventricular defibrillation lead carrying, at atrial level, two floating electrodes (atrial dipole). Atrial activity is thus recorded with a single lead. This allows detection of atrial arrhythmias (atrial high-rate episodes, subclinical AF), better VT–SVT discrimination and VDD operation. However, because the dipole is floating, it cannot pace the atrium. The MATRIX registry showed that atrial high-rate episodes can be followed on remote monitoring according to the recommended duration thresholds.
prog-bbm-037.aRetenir: DX = a single ICD lead with a floating atrial dipole: atrial sensing without atrial pacing.

prog-bbm-038.question: Regarding Biotronik VR-T DX ICDs, which statements are correct?
options: They are only indicated in patients who do not need atrial pacing
The low-amplitude atrial signal recorded by the floating dipole is amplified by the device (by a factor of 4)
They can operate in DDD(R) mode thanks to the floating atrial dipole
They allow conventional bipolar atrial pacing
commentaires: Correct: the manual restricts VR-T DX devices to patients who do not need atrial pacing.
Correct: the dipole does not touch the wall; atrial sensitivity is amplified by a factor of 4 to compensate.
Incorrect: the floating dipole senses but cannot pace; the available modes are VDD(R), VDI(R) and VVI(R).
Incorrect: atrial pacing is impossible with a floating dipole.
prog-bbm-038.explication: The Rivacor manual states that VR-T DX devices, and CRT-Ds using the DX function, are only indicated in patients who do not need atrial pacing. The floating dipole does not touch the wall: the atrial signal is smaller than with a fixed atrial lead. To compensate, the programmed atrial sensitivity is amplified by a factor of 4 in DX devices. The available modes are VDD(R) and VDI(R), in addition to VVI(R); DDD(R) is impossible since the atrium cannot be paced. The system is therefore unsuitable for sinus node dysfunction requiring atrial pacing.
prog-bbm-038.aRetenir: DX: ×4 atrial signal amplification, VDD mode possible, never atrial pacing (hence no DDD).

prog-bbm-039.question: In a patient with a Biotronik ProMRI pacemaker, what is the MRI AutoDetect function for?
options: Waiving the lead eligibility check if the device is ProMRI
Manual MRI programming before the scan, then reprogramming afterwards
A sensor detects the MRI field and toggles the MRI programme
Raising the pacing amplitude to 7.5 V during the scan, then lowering it
commentaires: Incorrect: the eligibility of the complete system (generator and leads, scan conditions) must still be checked according to the ProMRI manual.
Incorrect: this is the conventional procedure that MRI AutoDetect avoids: there is no longer any need for two interrogations on the day of the scan.
Correct: enabled for up to 14 days, MRI AutoDetect automatically switches to the MRI programme and then back to the permanent programme.
Incorrect: MRI AutoDetect does not change the amplitude by itself; it activates a preset MRI programme.
prog-bbm-039.explication: ProMRI devices have a sensor that recognises the static magnetic field of the MRI scanner. During an interrogation, MRI AutoDetect is enabled for a maximum of 14 days: if the patient undergoes the MRI within this window, the device activates the preset MRI programme, then automatically returns to the permanent programme after the scan. This avoids two interrogations on the same day, but does not remove the need to check the eligibility of the complete system (compatible generator and leads, scan conditions) according to the ProMRI manual. Programming tailored to the patient is still required (e.g. asynchronous mode in a pacing-dependent patient).
prog-bbm-039.aRetenir: MRI AutoDetect: window of up to 14 days, automatic switch to the MRI programme and back.

prog-bbm-040.question: The BIOTRONIK BIOMONITOR III implantable loop recorder, remotely monitored daily via Home Monitoring, can also deliver backup bradycardia pacing in the event of a prolonged pause.
options: True
False
commentaires: Incorrect: the BIOMONITOR III, like any implantable monitor, neither paces nor defibrillates.
Correct: it is a purely diagnostic implantable loop recorder, remotely monitored daily via Home Monitoring.
prog-bbm-040.explication: The BIOMONITOR III is a miniaturised insertable cardiac monitor with a long sensing vector (about 70 mm) to improve signal quality, particularly P-wave visibility. It is inserted in a single step with a dedicated tool (median procedure time of 4 minutes in the study by Deneke et al.) and includes automatic daily Home Monitoring. Like any implantable monitor, it is purely diagnostic: it neither paces nor defibrillates, hence the answer "False". It is used for recurrent unexplained syncope, infrequent palpitations or detection of AF after cryptogenic stroke.
prog-bbm-040.aRetenir: BIOMONITOR = purely diagnostic implantable loop recorder (no pacing), remotely monitored daily via Home Monitoring.

prog-bbm-041.question: What is the principle of the SafeR mode (formerly AAIsafeR) in MicroPort (formerly Sorin/ELA) pacemakers?
options: AAI monitoring conduction (ADI), temporary DDD if block or pause
DDD with an extended AV delay adjusted to the last 8 PR intervals (pseudo-AAI)
AAI(R) with a VVI backup running below the basic rate
DDD with negative AV hysteresis to maintain ventricular pacing
commentaires: Correct: SafeR paces in AAI while monitoring conduction (ADI) and switches temporarily to DDD in the event of AV block or a pause.
Incorrect: DDD with an automatically adjusted extended AV delay is Dplus mode, the other MicroPort algorithm.
Incorrect: AAI(R) with a slower VVI backup is RYTHMIQ (Boston Scientific).
Incorrect: negative AV hysteresis aims for the opposite (more ventricular pacing), in CRT.
prog-bbm-041.explication: SafeR provides AAI pacing while continuously monitoring AV conduction (ADI operation). When AV block (complete, second-degree or first-degree) or a ventricular pause occurs, the device switches temporarily to DDD with the programmed AV delay. In DDD, it periodically checks whether conduction has returned so that it can revert to AAI. SafeR is aimed mainly at patients with sinus node dysfunction or paroxysmal conduction disorders. It differs from Dplus, which remains in DDD with an extended AV delay, and from Boston Scientific RYTHMIQ, which runs a VVI backup underneath AAI(R). In the ANSWER trial, SafeR reduced ventricular pacing to about 11% versus 94% in DDD.
prog-bbm-041.aRetenir: SafeR = AAI with conduction monitoring and a temporary switch to DDD in the event of block or pause.

prog-bbm-042.question: Which of the following criteria temporarily switch SafeR from AAI to DDD?
options: 2 consecutive blocked atrial events (complete AV block criterion)
3 blocked atrial events within the last 12 cycles (second-degree AV block criterion)
3 slow ventricular beats within a window of 11 cycles
A ventricular pause longer than the programmed value (2, 3 or 4 s)
A single premature ventricular contraction
commentaires: Correct: 2 consecutive blocked P waves define the SafeR complete AV block criterion.
Correct: 3 blocked P waves within 12 cycles define the second-degree AV block criterion.
Incorrect: 3 slow beats out of 11 is the RYTHMIQ switching criterion (Boston Scientific); the fourth SafeR criterion is 6 consecutive long PR intervals.
Correct: a pause longer than the programmed value (3 s as shipped) triggers a switch to DDD.
Incorrect: an isolated PVC simply restarts the escape interval in AAI.
prog-bbm-042.explication: SafeR switches from AAI to DDD according to four criteria. Complete AV block: 2 consecutive blocked atrial events. Second-degree AV block: 3 blocked atrial events within the last 12 cycles. First-degree AV block: 6 consecutive PR or AR intervals longer than the programmed value. Ventricular pause: a pause longer than the programmed value (2, 3 or 4 s; 3 s as shipped). A P wave is considered blocked when no ventricular event is sensed within the atrial cycle. The first-degree AV block criterion can be restricted to exercise ("exercise only"). Counting slow beats over an 11-cycle window belongs to Boston Scientific RYTHMIQ. An isolated PVC does not trigger a switch: it simply restarts the escape interval in AAI.
prog-bbm-042.aRetenir: SafeR switches to DDD on complete AV block (2 blocked P waves), second-degree AV block (3/12), first-degree AV block (6 long PR intervals) or a pause.

prog-bbm-043.question: After a temporary SafeR switch to DDD, when does the MicroPort device return to AAI?
options: After 25 cycles of AV hysteresis with fewer than 2 V-paced beats out of 10
After 6 consecutive cycles with intrinsic ventricular sensing
After 12 consecutive intrinsic R waves, or a test every 100 paced cycles
Conduction test at 1 min, then at doubling intervals up to 16 h at most
commentaires: Incorrect: this is the condition for RYTHMIQ to return to AAI(R), via AV Search+ (Boston Scientific).
Incorrect: 6 consecutive Vs is the standard setting for entering ADI with Vp Suppression (Biotronik).
Correct: SafeR returns to AAI after 12 consecutive intrinsic ventricular events, or tests conduction every 100 paced cycles.
Incorrect: tests at doubling intervals up to 16 h are those of Medtronic MVP.
prog-bbm-043.explication: In DDD, SafeR returns to AAI as soon as it senses 12 consecutive intrinsic ventricular events, proof that conduction has recovered. Otherwise, it automatically reverts to AAI every 100 paced ventricular cycles to test conduction. If the block persists, a switching criterion (often the complete AV block criterion) immediately brings it back to DDD. This is why a Holter may show regular AAI "attempts" followed by 2 blocked P waves: this is normal operation, not a malfunction. If blocks are very frequent, a long-term switch mode takes over. Other manufacturers have their own rules: tests at doubling intervals for Medtronic MVP, AV Search+ for Boston Scientific RYTHMIQ, 6 consecutive Vs for Biotronik Vp Suppression.
prog-bbm-043.aRetenir: Return to AAI: 12 consecutive intrinsic R waves, or an automatic test every 100 paced cycles.

prog-bbm-044.question: In which situations does SafeR remain in DDD until 8 a.m. the next morning, and how can it leave DDD earlier?
prog-bbm-044.reponseAttendue: Long-term switch if: 45 or more AV block episodes in the last 24 h, or 15 or more episodes per 24 h for 3 consecutive days, or at least 50% DDD pacing over one hour. The automatic tests every 100 cycles are then suspended; only 12 consecutive intrinsic R waves bring it back to AAI before 8 a.m., otherwise it retests AAI at 8 a.m.
prog-bbm-044.explication: When blocks are frequent, constantly switching between AAI and DDD serves no purpose and may cause symptoms. SafeR therefore defines a long-term switch: at least 45 AV block episodes in 24 h, at least 15 episodes per 24 h for 3 consecutive days, or at least 50% DDD over one hour. It then stays in DDD until 8 a.m. the next day, suspending the periodic tests every 100 cycles. It only reverts to AAI before 8 a.m. if it senses 12 consecutive intrinsic R waves. Similarly, during exercise, after 3 switches it stays in DDD until the end of exercise. Knowing these rules avoids wrongly concluding that the algorithm has failed when faced with prolonged DDD pacing.
prog-bbm-044.aRetenir: Frequent blocks: SafeR stays in DDD until 8 a.m. the next day, unless 12 intrinsic R waves return.

prog-bbm-045.question: What did the randomised ANSWER trial (SafeR versus DDD, 650 patients enrolled, 3-year follow-up) show?
options: More syncope and deaths with SafeR, attributed to pauses tolerated in AAI
A significant 50% reduction in permanent AF on the primary endpoint
Less persistent AF (relative reduction of about 40%), no effect on mortality
Much less V pacing (11.5% vs 93.6%), primary endpoint not significant
commentaires: Incorrect: there was no excess of deaths or of syncope with SafeR.
Incorrect: the composite primary endpoint did not differ significantly (HR 0.78, p = 0.30).
Incorrect: a relative reduction of about 40% in persistent AF is the result of SAVE PACe, not ANSWER.
Correct: 11.5% vs 93.6% V pacing at 3 years, with no significant difference in the composite primary endpoint.
prog-bbm-045.explication: ANSWER compared SafeR with standard DDD in patients with sinus node dysfunction or AV block. Ventricular pacing was massively reduced (11.5% vs 93.6% at 3 years). However, the composite co-primary endpoint (hospitalisation for heart failure, AF or cardioversion) did not differ significantly (HR 0.78, p = 0.30). On secondary endpoints, SafeR reduced the risk of cardiac death or heart failure hospitalisation by 51% and cardiovascular hospitalisations by 30%. There was no excess of deaths or of syncope. The reduction of about 40% in persistent AF is the result of SAVE PACe, a different trial. A distinction must therefore be made between the proven benefit on RV pacing and the benefit on clinical events, which is only suggested by secondary endpoints.
prog-bbm-045.aRetenir: ANSWER: SafeR markedly reduces RV pacing, with no significant effect on the composite primary endpoint.

prog-bbm-046.question: At a follow-up visit, the Holter of a MicroPort patient programmed in SafeR shows an isolated sinus P wave not followed by a QRS, with no ventricular spike, after which 1:1 conduction resumes with a normal PR interval. The patient is asymptomatic. How should this be interpreted?
options: Intermittent loss of ventricular capture: check the V threshold
Normal function: an isolated blocked P wave is tolerated in AAI
Failure to switch to DDD, which should have occurred at this blocked P wave
Ventricular undersensing by the device: plan a lead revision
commentaires: Incorrect: loss of capture would show a V spike not followed by a QRS; here there is no V spike.
Correct: an isolated blocked P wave does not meet any switching criterion; SafeR tolerates it in AAI.
Incorrect: 2 consecutive blocked P waves or 3 within 12 cycles are required to switch to DDD; a single one is not enough.
Incorrect: no QRS was missed; the absence of a V spike is expected in AAI.
prog-bbm-046.explication: In AAI, SafeR does not pace the ventricle after every P wave: it only monitors conduction. An isolated blocked P wave does not meet any switching criterion (complete AV block: 2 consecutive blocked P waves; second-degree AV block: 3 within 12 cycles). The absence of a ventricular spike is therefore normal and suggests neither undersensing nor loss of capture: with loss of capture, a V spike not followed by a QRS would be seen. This behaviour must be recognised to avoid wrongly diagnosing a malfunction. If the patient becomes symptomatic or blocks recur, the switching criteria take over.
prog-bbm-046.aRetenir: In SafeR, an isolated blocked P wave with no V spike is normal function.

prog-bbm-047.question: In SafeR, while an atrial arrhythmia is suspected, the three AV block criteria are suspended and only a ventricular pause can trigger a switch to DDD; the pause value is then automatically reduced to 2 seconds (except in REPLY).
options: True
False
commentaires: Correct: when an atrial arrhythmia is suspected (WARAD), only the pause criterion remains active, reduced to 2 s (except in REPLY).
Incorrect: counting blocked P waves makes no sense during an atrial arrhythmia; the three AV block criteria are indeed suspended.
prog-bbm-047.explication: During an atrial arrhythmia, counting "blocked P waves" makes no sense: conduction is inevitably irregular or partial. As soon as an atrial arrhythmia is suspected (WARAD), SafeR therefore suspends the complete, second-degree and first-degree AV block criteria. Only the ventricular pause criterion remains active, and its value is reduced to 2 s (except in REPLY). If the arrhythmia is conducted, the device switches directly from AAI to DDI via the Fallback Mode Switch. If it is not conducted, it first switches to DDD on the pause criterion, then to DDI once fallback is confirmed.
prog-bbm-047.aRetenir: SafeR during atrial arrhythmia: only the pause criterion (2 s) remains active, followed by fallback to DDI.

prog-bbm-048.question: What is the principle of Dplus mode in MicroPort pacemakers?
options: Shortening the AV delay to ensure biventricular pacing
A true AAI mode with ventricular monitoring and a switch to DDD
Automatic AV delay hysteresis promoting intrinsic conduction
Reduced-rate backup VVI pacing running underneath AAI(R)
commentaires: Incorrect: shortening the AV delay for CRT is negative AV hysteresis, which has the opposite aim.
Incorrect: a true AAI mode with monitoring and a switch to DDD describes SafeR; Dplus remains in DDD.
Correct: Dplus remains in DDD with an extended AV delay (pseudo-AAI) adjusted to the last 8 PR or AR intervals.
Incorrect: reduced-rate backup VVI underneath AAI(R) is RYTHMIQ (Boston Scientific).
prog-bbm-048.explication: MicroPort presents Dplus as an automatic AV delay hysteresis algorithm designed to promote intrinsic AV conduction. Unlike SafeR, Dplus does not rely on a true AAI mode: the device remains in DDD, with an extended AV delay (the so-called pseudo-AAI phase) automatically adjusted from the last 8 measured PR or AR intervals, so that the intrinsic QRS can occur before ventricular pacing. If ventricular pacing becomes necessary again, it returns to an appropriate AV delay. As with any long AV delay, attention must be paid to unfavourable AV timing if the PR interval is very long.
prog-bbm-048.aRetenir: Dplus = DDD with automatic AV delay hysteresis (pseudo-AAI) to promote intrinsic conduction.

prog-bbm-049.question: According to the PARAD decision tree (MicroPort dual-chamber ICDs), which criteria → conclusion pairings are correct?
options: Unstable R-R → atrial fibrillation, no therapy
Stable R-R without P-R association → ventricular tachycardia, therapy
Stable R-R with N:1 association → ventricular tachycardia, therapy
Stable R-R with 1:1 association and atrial-origin acceleration → VT, therapy
commentaires: Correct: an unstable rhythm is classified as AF and is not treated.
Correct: a stable rhythm without P-R association is classified as VT and treated.
Incorrect: a stable N:1 association is classified as atrial flutter, with no therapy.
Incorrect: with 1:1 association, acceleration of atrial origin points to SVT, not VT.
prog-bbm-049.explication: PARAD (P And R based Arrhythmia Detection) analyses the last 8 cycles on every beat once a majority of cycles fall within the tachycardia zone. It first tests R-R stability: an unstable rhythm is classified as AF and not treated. A stable rhythm without P-R association is classified as VT and treated. A stable rhythm with N:1 association is classified as atrial flutter and not treated. With 1:1 association, the decisive criterion is the origin of the acceleration: atrial (SVT) or gradual with no acceleration (sinus tachycardia), no therapy; ventricular, VT and therapy. Mistaking N:1 association for dissociation, or reversing the origin of the acceleration, are the two classic errors.
prog-bbm-049.aRetenir: PARAD: unstable = AF; stable and dissociated = VT; N:1 = flutter; 1:1 = look at the origin of the acceleration.

prog-bbm-050.question: What is the only difference between PARAD and PARAD+ in MicroPort ICDs?
options: Searching for long cycles suggesting AF in a stable, dissociated rhythm
Adding QRS morphology analysis against a reference template
Removing the R-R stability criterion, considered insufficiently specific
Analysing the origin of the acceleration when there is 1:1 association
commentaires: Correct: a cycle longer than the mean of the last 4 plus a programmable gap raises suspicion of AF and delays therapy by 24 cycles.
Incorrect: PARAD+ adds no morphology analysis; template comparison is the principle of other discriminators (MorphMatch, Wavelet).
Incorrect: the stability criterion remains the first step of the decision tree.
Incorrect: the origin of the acceleration with 1:1 association is already analysed by PARAD; that is not the difference.
prog-bbm-050.explication: With PARAD, some patients in AF received inappropriate therapies: the ventricular response appeared stable and, in the absence of a stable P-R association, the rhythm was classified as VT. Yet these AF episodes regularly included longer ventricular cycles, at least every 20 cycles. PARAD+ looks for these long cycles when the rhythm is stable but not associated: a cycle longer than the mean of the last 4 cycles plus a programmable gap (Long Cycle Gap) raises suspicion of AF and delays therapy by 24 cycles. If no long cycle appears within 24 cycles, VT is confirmed and treated. The MicroPort implementation of the 2019 consensus uses a gap of 170 ms.
prog-bbm-050.aRetenir: PARAD+ = PARAD + a search for long cycles, to avoid treating AF with a pseudo-regular response.

prog-bbm-051.question: According to the MicroPort implementation of the 2019 ICD programming consensus update, which detection programming is suggested in a patient with no history of VT?
options: VF > 200 bpm with 8 cycles, VT 150 bpm, no monitor zone
VF > 255 bpm, fast VT 230 bpm, VT 185 bpm, slow VT monitor zone
VF 231 bpm (30/40 intervals), VT2 188 bpm (30 intervals), VT1 monitor
VF ≥ 250 bpm (5 s), VT ≥ 185 bpm (12 s), optional VT-1 monitor zone
commentaires: Incorrect: short detection at a low rate is the conventional programming that the consensus aims to avoid.
Correct: VF > 255 bpm (20 cycles + 6/8 majority), fast VT 230 bpm, VT 185 bpm, optional slow VT monitor zone.
Incorrect: 231 bpm with 30/40 and 188 bpm with 30 intervals are the settings of the Biotronik implementation.
Incorrect: 250 bpm (5 s) and 185 bpm (12 s) are the settings of the Boston Scientific implementation.
prog-bbm-051.explication: The MicroPort appendix of the 2019 update suggests: VF above 255 bpm (20 cycles and 6/8 majority), fast VT at 230 bpm, VT at 185 bpm (20 or 30 cycles and 6/8 majority), and an optional slow VT monitor zone. Shocks in the VF zone are set at 42 J (6 shocks). In dual-chamber devices and CRT-Ds, discrimination relies on PARAD+ (onset 25%, stability 65 ms, long cycle extension 10 cycles, long cycle gap 170 ms).
