For dual-chamber pacing, the appendix suggests SafeR; in CRT, weekly SonR optimisation if a SonRtip lead is implanted. The common principle remains raising rate cut-offs and prolonging detection.
prog-bbm-051.aRetenir: MicroPort 2019: VF > 255 bpm, fast VT 230 bpm, VT 185 bpm, PARAD+ in dual-chamber devices.

prog-bbm-052.question: What is MicroPort's SonR optimisation of cardiac resynchronisation based on?
options: Intracardiac ventricular impedance, reflecting contractility
The intrinsic AV interval measured periodically, minus a programmable offset
Intervals measured on intracardiac EGMs, without a dedicated sensor
A micro-accelerometer in the SonRtip atrial lead, correlated with dP/dt max
commentaires: Incorrect: intracardiac impedance is the signal of Biotronik Closed Loop Stimulation, a rate response sensor.
Incorrect: intrinsic AV minus an offset is the principle of SyncAV (Abbott).
Incorrect: calculation from EGM intervals is SmartDelay (Boston Scientific).
Correct: the micro-accelerometer in the SonRtip lead measures endocardial acceleration, correlated with dP/dt max, to optimise AV and VV delays.
prog-bbm-052.explication: The SonR sensor is a micro-accelerometer located in the tip of the SonRtip atrial lead. It measures the vibrations produced by contraction (peak endocardial acceleration), which correlate well with LV dP/dt max, an index of contractility. The device varies the AV and VV delays and selects those that give the best SonR signal. This optimisation is automatic and repeated every week without echocardiography: the VV delay is optimised at rest, the AV delays at rest and during exercise. It is only possible with the SonRtip lead. Other manufacturers proceed differently: SmartDelay (Boston Scientific) from EGMs, SyncAV (Abbott) from the intrinsic AV interval; the intracardiac impedance of CLS (Biotronik) is used for rate response.
prog-bbm-052.aRetenir: SonR = accelerometer in the SonRtip atrial lead, weekly automatic optimisation of AV/VV delays.

prog-bbm-053.question: What was the result of the RESPOND-CRT trial (SonR optimisation versus echocardiographic optimisation)?
options: Superiority of SonR for all-cause mortality, with almost 50% fewer deaths
No better than a fixed 120 ms AV delay on LV end-systolic volume
Inferiority of SonR to echocardiography on the clinical responder rate
Non-inferiority for 12-month response, fewer HF hospitalisations
commentaires: Incorrect: no mortality benefit was demonstrated.
Incorrect: this is the result of SMART-AV (SmartDelay); RESPOND-CRT compared SonR with echocardiography on clinical response.
Incorrect: SonR achieved non-inferiority (75.0% vs 70.4% responders).
Correct: non-inferiority (75.0% vs 70.4%) and a 35% reduction in the risk of HF hospitalisation (HR 0.65).
prog-bbm-053.explication: RESPOND-CRT randomised 998 patients (2:1) to weekly automatic AV/VV delay optimisation by SonR or echocardiographic optimisation. The primary endpoint was the clinical responder rate at 12 months: alive, free of adjudicated heart failure events, with improvement in NYHA class or quality of life. SonR achieved non-inferiority (75.0% vs 70.4%). Over a mean follow-up of about 18 months, it was associated with a 35% reduction in the risk of heart failure hospitalisation (HR 0.65). No mortality benefit was demonstrated.
prog-bbm-053.aRetenir: RESPOND-CRT: SonR non-inferior to echocardiography, with fewer heart failure hospitalisations.

prog-bbm-054.question: A SonR-compatible MicroPort CRT-D can perform weekly automatic SonR optimisation of AV and VV delays whatever atrial lead is implanted, including a standard atrial lead.
options: True
False
commentaires: Incorrect: without a SonRtip lead, whose tip contains the micro-accelerometer, there is no SonR signal.
Correct: SonR optimisation requires the SonRtip atrial lead; a standard atrial lead does not allow it.
prog-bbm-054.explication: This is false: the SonR algorithm is only available with the SonRtip atrial lead, whose tip contains the micro-accelerometer; without it, there is no SonR signal. When programmed to "AV+VV", automatic SonR optimisation calculates the optimal VV delay at rest and the optimal AV delays at rest and during exercise, every week. The first optimisation starts at midnight on the day of activation, then every Monday at midnight. Resting measurements require stable conditions: rate below 90 bpm, no ectopic beats and no tachyarrhythmia. This weekly schedule makes it possible to follow ventricular remodelling without repeated echocardiograms.
prog-bbm-054.aRetenir: No SonRtip lead, no SonR; with it, weekly optimisation of the VV delay at rest and of the AV delay at rest and during exercise.

prog-bbm-055.question: In a MicroPort pacemaker, how does the Fallback Mode Switch (FMS) work?
options: Switch to AAI(R) with VVI backup for the whole duration of the arrhythmia
WARAD suspicion, 28-of-32 confirmation, then fallback to DDI(R)
Fallback to VVI(R) as soon as the atrial rate exceeds the maximum rate
Fallback once an entry counter is met, with a gradual decrease in rate
commentaires: Incorrect: AAI(R) with VVI backup is RYTHMIQ; an atrial arrhythmia cannot be managed in AAI.
Correct: suspicion via the WARAD, 28/32 confirmation (main criterion), fallback to DDI(R), then return to the programmed mode.
Incorrect: fallback is to DDI(R), independently of the programmed maximum rate, after a confirmation phase.
Incorrect: an entry counter with a gradual decrease in rate is the logic of Boston Scientific ATR.
prog-bbm-055.explication: FMS avoids high-rate ventricular pacing during a tracked atrial arrhythmia. A premature atrial event falling within the WARAD (Window of Atrial Rate Acceleration Detection) puts the device into the suspicion phase; the paced ventricular rate is then capped at 120 bpm (or at the programmed maximum rate if lower) and the AV delay is shortened to improve atrial sensing. Main confirmation criterion: at least 28 suspect cycles out of 32 ventricular cycles (about 15 s). A secondary criterion (18 of 32, twice in a row) deals with atrial undersensing. Fallback is to DDI(R), independently of the programmed maximum rate, and the device returns to the initial mode when the arrhythmia stops. Boston Scientific ATR is based on a different logic (entry and duration counters).
prog-bbm-055.aRetenir: MicroPort FMS: suspicion via the WARAD, 28/32 confirmation, fallback to DDI(R).

prog-bbm-056.question: In some MicroPort pacemakers (notably REPLY, KORA, ENO and TEO), programming SafeR mode automatically disables ventricular Autothreshold.
options: True
False
commentaires: Correct: the SafeR documentation states that ventricular Autothreshold is set to OFF in these models, and that FMS is set to ON.
Incorrect: this is well documented; the threshold must then be checked and the ventricular amplitude set manually with an adequate margin.
prog-bbm-056.explication: MicroPort's SafeR technical documentation states that when SafeR is programmed, ventricular Autothreshold is automatically set to OFF in REPLY, KORA, ENO, TEO, PARADYM RF, INTENSIA and PLATINIUM, and that FMS is automatically set to ON. The documentation does not explain the reason for this constraint; remember the practical consequence: in these models, the threshold must be checked and the ventricular amplitude programmed manually, with an adequate safety margin, since the ventricle will be paced during switches to DDD. Otherwise, Autothreshold (ventricular RVAT and atrial RAAT) remains a way of maintaining capture while preserving the battery.
prog-bbm-056.aRetenir: In several MicroPort models, SafeR disables ventricular Autothreshold: set the V amplitude manually.

prog-bbm-057.question: What is the name of MicroPort's remote monitoring solution for pacemakers and defibrillators?
options: SmartView
Home Monitoring
CareLink
LATITUDE
commentaires: Correct: SmartView (bedside monitor or SmartView Connect app) is the MicroPort CRM solution.
Incorrect: Home Monitoring is Biotronik's remote monitoring system.
Incorrect: CareLink is Medtronic's remote monitoring system.
Incorrect: LATITUDE is Boston Scientific's remote monitoring system.
prog-bbm-057.explication: SmartView is MicroPort CRM's remote monitoring solution: a bedside monitor (SmartView, then SmartView Connect) and, for Bluetooth-compatible devices, the SmartView Connect mobile app on the patient's smartphone. It transmits device data and alerts to the platform reviewed by the team. LATITUDE is the Boston Scientific solution, Home Monitoring the Biotronik one and CareLink the Medtronic one. Knowing each manufacturer's system is useful for organising follow-up and transmissions after implantation. The 2023 HRS consensus statement recommends remote monitoring for all device recipients, whatever the manufacturer.
prog-bbm-057.aRetenir: MicroPort remote monitoring = SmartView (monitor or SmartView Connect app).
